title: GPU-first rendering
objective: Make the GPU the renderer of record for the picture, the histogram, samples and export, with correctness a declared tolerance against a whole-frame CPU reference, so that an ordinary edit of a 16 to 60 MP photograph is one path at every zoom and the proxies, windows, point tiles, estimate stores, settle phases and fallbacks that made the CPU path fast enough can be deleted.
context_summary: The decision (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering) rests on the cost of the CPU renderer and the machinery around it, which can stall the editor for minutes on the CPU point path: at the baseline in docs/design/gpu-first.md, 29,850 lines of CPU render against 5,937 of GPU programs, 11 GPU and 18 window fallback reasons and 8 caches. Every module has a GPU program. The plan converges in stages that each delete something: every zoom on the GPU; the picture at rest and the histogram on the GPU; per-frame estimates; samples and export through GPU tiles; portability, warm-up and the retirement of the CPU production paths; one qualification and measurement at the end. Constraints: textures are tiled past 8192 px, the GPU budgets stay, a machine without a GPU gets the reference renderer with a notice, and the tolerance per output kind is measured before any stage lands. The design is docs/design/gpu-first.md.

tasks.description: Build the reference comparison harness, measure the tolerance per output kind on the corpus, and rewrite the rules and testing guidance for reference-buffer correctness.
extra_context: Correctness is a declared tolerance against the CPU reference render for every output kind (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering). Before any stage lands, one harness must render a stack on the reference and on the GPU and report, per output kind, the error against the limits in the design: the preview error limit for the picture, the histogram limits for its bins and clipping counts, the display limit per pixel for export, equality by construction for samples.

Start from the existing qualification machinery (crates/luxforge-core/src/render/gpu qualification, the corpus and the error limit in docs/design/gpu-preview.md, xtask gpu_qualification) and extend it to the histogram reduction, export and the at-rest picture. The harness runs natively; on CI it runs the reference renderer's own tests and, on Linux, the software Vulkan adapter when TASK-008 lands.

Docs to rewrite with the measured limits: performance rule 4's exception and rule 11, rule 14's cache list, the review checklist's exactness items, docs/engineering/development.md's evidence rules (exact-buffer tests become reference-buffer tests with a declared tolerance), docs/design/architecture.md's renderer section. AGENTS.md's pillars already state the decision; keep them in step.

Delivered: `cargo xtask gpu-qualification` is the release gate in the `rendered` tier (docs/engineering/development.md). It measures the picture on the whole corpus at Fit, 33%, 50% and 100% (docs/specs/performance.md, GPU qualification against the reference), passes under the recorded default (the picture in motion held to the frame it settles to) and fails with `--hold-motion-to-reference` on 481 of 750 cells below 100%.

tasks.description: Render the picture at rest on the GPU: commits, history, presets and Compare draw through the same programs as a drag, at Fit from the source mip chain and at 100% from the window, and the CPU proxy phase leaves the preview path (stage 2).
extra_context: With the GPU as the renderer of record the picture at rest is the GPU's own frame of the committed stack, and the CPU proxy phase (docs/design/instant-preview.md, Fit proxy and exact phases), the restoration-prefix cache (crates/luxforge-core/src/preview/restoration.rs) and Detail's settled-from-exact display (FitSettle::Exact, downscale_raster) leave this path.

The at-rest picture must meet the display limit against the reference reduced to the view's size, on the corpus, at Fit, below 100% and at 100%; in the label vocabulary nothing at rest is called approximate, and the status bar's render figure is the GPU frame's.
Compare and history return draw the retained content on the GPU in one frame, so no retained-frame re-adoption is needed. The settle dissolve keeps its form, between two GPU frames.

Detail's exact-settle progress bar loses its subject on this path; keep its machinery for export and any job longer than a second, or retire it with the exact phase in stage 5, and say which in the Detail design.

Recorded default (docs/design/gpu-first.md, Proposals with recorded defaults): a frame processed over a source reduced to the view's size misses the limit against the reference on 475 of 744 cells below 100%, so the picture at rest at Fit and below 100% is process-first, the stack at full resolution in tiles reduced to the view's size, which meets every limit; the source's reduction (a box pass over the GPU-resident source, or its mip chain) serves the drag's boundary, whose frame is held to the at-rest frame it settles to.

Delivered: with no gesture open the GPU draws the committed stack after a commit, a history selection, a preset, Compare and an open, its view plan at once and at Fit and below 100% its tiles at full resolution reduced to the view, dissolving in; every boundary is derived on the GPU from the source it holds; the proxy phase, the restoration-prefix cache and Detail's settled-from-exact display are deleted. The release gate draws the editor's own frames and gates the picture at rest within its limit on every cell; the picture in motion below 100% is reported, not gated, past a limit on 481 of 750 cells against either the picture at rest or the reference (docs/decisions.md).

tasks.description: Compute the histogram and clipping counts on the GPU: a reduction over the full stage rendered in tiles after each commit and release, and over the displayed frame during motion, labelled updating; the CPU exact phase and the quiet-settle whole-frame render leave the preview path (stage 2).
extra_context: On the GPU the counts are a reduction over full-resolution tiles of the stack rendered with halos, inside the GPU budget, run after each commit and release; during motion the counts come from the displayed frame and the inspector says updating, as docs/decisions.md, Interactive previews at 100%, allows. The report keeps its shape, identity and the owner's cache so an API client's `analysis.request` is a hit.
The quiet timer stays for 100% region refinement only if stage 5 still needs it.

The full-stage tiles stage 2's at-rest picture renders (TASK-003, process-first) are the reduction's renderer: the counts are one more reduction over the same tiles, run after each commit and release.

Delivered: a committed stack the GPU presents is counted from its own tiles at full resolution (at 100% and above the same tiles drawn for their counts alone) with no CPU frame rendered or reduced, the counts reaching the owner's analysis cache in the report's shape; during motion the counts come from the tick's output, labelled updating; the quiet-settle whole-frame render is deleted. The tolerance is the earth mover's distance at most 0.25 code per channel and luminance and each clipping count within 0.1% of the output pixel count against the reference, met on every corpus stack (largest 0.13 code).

tasks.description: Compute global estimates on the GPU per frame from a reduced stage the GPU holds, and retire the estimate store, the reduced-grid store and the estimate fallbacks (stage 3).
extra_context: On the GPU the drafted prefix's reduced stage is a mip-level render of the colour run over the reduced source planes, a fraction of a megapixel at 60 MP, computed per frame; the light and the grid follow from it on the GPU. For a Detail prefix the reduced stage is Detail's output reduced, which the design of Detail measured to barely move the light; the harness measures it against the reference's exact light on the corpus, and the display limit decides.
With estimates per frame the stores, their keys, their eviction tests and the three fallbacks go, as does the window planner's refusal of the cut behind an estimating unit.

Delivered: every view's plan and the desktop's tile worker compute Dehaze's light on the GPU per frame from the full-resolution source through light links run before the chain; the GPU estimate plumbing, the region-estimate and window-estimate fallbacks, EstimateAfterSpatial and the Dehaze notice class are deleted. The release gate holds the picture at rest within its limit on every cell and every export to the reference export on every stack, all drawn on the GPU. The exact light behind Detail or an earlier Presence layer is TASK-012's, through the staged sweeps; the CPU estimate and reduced-grid stores are TASK-010's.

tasks.description: Answer render.sample, mask.sample-input, the neutral picker and brush seeds from a GPU tile render, and retire the point worker and the point-tile cache (stage 4).
extra_context: On the GPU a sample is one tile of the stack rendered at full resolution with its halos and one pixel read back; a pick's 25 points share one tile set. The owner plans in O(layers) and hands the read to a GPU worker that owns a device queue; the answer carries the same identity fields.

The sample equals the byte on screen at that pixel by construction when the view shows that tile at 100%, and otherwise the rendered tile's byte; against the reference it is within the display limit. The raw-panel and histogram scenarios tie their pixels through `render.sample` as api steps.
Retire PointTiles, the point worker, the parked pixel-read rounds and the point-sample rows of the known costs; rule 4's exception becomes a sentence.

Delivered: render.sample, the neutral pick, mask.sample-input, a colour-limited stroke's seed and edit.set-pixel are planned on the owner and read by its tile service, the desktop's GPU tile worker or the reference for a host without one, each answer naming its renderer; the point worker, PointTiles and the per-read round loop are deleted. Every corpus sample is within its limit and equal to the byte on screen, 6,250 of 6,250 on 250 stacks. A mutation parks once per pixel its plans read, at most four (docs/decisions.md); the renderer field, cross-machine seeds and the RAW neutral patch on the owner are described in docs/design/gpu-first.md. The sample timing is TASK-011's.

tasks.description: Export through GPU tiles: export.jpeg renders full-resolution tiles on the GPU and encodes them, with the reference renderer as the export for machines without a GPU and as an explicit reference option (stage 4).

tasks.description: Make the renderer of record portable and testable without a native GPU: a software Vulkan adapter for Linux CI journeys, the reference renderer as the no-GPU fallback with a notice, and the native checks Windows and Linux need.
extra_context: The pillars require Windows and Linux portability and distinguish VM functional checks from native GPU evidence. wgpu selects a software adapter (lavapipe) on Linux when no device is present; macOS has no software Metal, so a macOS VM proves the reference renderer and the owner thread, not the GPU.

A machine whose adapter is missing, refused or fails compilation gets the reference renderer: whole frames at rest and labelled display-sized CPU proxy frames during a drag, named in the status bar and the API's session. CI runs the reference tests and, on Linux, the rendered journeys through the software adapter; the development guide's CI section records exactly what each lane proves.

The forced --no-gpu-render launch shows the reference renderer notice in the status bar and session.state, every frame is the CPU path with the reason recorded, and the no-gpu-render scenario and tests prove it on the M4. Hosted Linux no-adapter checks, release acceptance and packaging pass. The lavapipe lane runs ten functional journeys: empty, load, replacement, invalid, repeated, alternating, histogram, gpu-identity, gpu-preview and no-gpu-render; every retained journey runs before aggregate failure and checks that each successful launch recorded only Cpu adapters. Photo-sized large24 and large60 stay in native rendered verification; the forced reference-renderer journey keeps its 24 MP fixture. A passing hosted result for the retained software-adapter journeys remains open, as do native Windows/Linux checks.

lavapipe misses the drag thresholds (docs/specs/performance.md, Software adapters), so the software-adapter fallback is built behind --software-adapter and off by default, and a session without a GPU keeps the CPU display-sized proxy for drags (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering).

tasks.description: Warm the GPU program set in the background at launch and open, so the first picture never waits on a cold shader cache, with the reference renderer labelled until then.
extra_context: On a cold Metal cache, as after an update, a Presence drag's sequences take seconds to compile (docs/specs/performance.md, Presence and Detail sequences in the editor); with the GPU as the renderer of record the picture at rest would wait on that compilation.

Warm the programs the open stack needs first, then the rest, on the GPU compile thread, with the reference frame on screen and labelled until the GPU frame replaces it; record the warm-up's duration in the Performance section and the events.

Delivered: each committed job compiles the picture on screen first, then the open stack's drags, then every module's first drag, Detail and Presence included; while the picture at rest compiles the reference frame is on screen and the status bar says Preparing GPU render; the warm-up is listed on the activity board as gpu.warm and recorded as the gpu_warm_up event, its duration in docs/specs/performance.md, Warming at launch and open. A release that changes which units a layer uses still compiles one link of its picture at rest (docs/design/gpu-first.md).

tasks.description: Qualify and measure the GPU-first editor on a quiet host: the corpus comparison per output kind as the release gate, and the latencies against the baseline.
extra_context: Rule 13: release build, quiet host, 30 samples where a distribution is claimed, load recorded around every run. Measure: a tick and a commit on the 16 MP Air 2S stack of the design at Fit, 33% and 100%; the histogram after a commit; a three-segment sample warm and cold; an export at 24 and 60 MP; a cold-cache first picture; Compare toggle; a RAW white-balance release. Compare each with the baseline table in the design.

Run the harness on the M4 and on any Windows or Linux machine with a GPU the owner supplies; record what each machine proved. Update docs/specs/performance.md, the known costs, the roadmap and feature status; delete this plan when the outcome is recorded.

Measured on the M4 (release, quiet host; docs/specs/performance.md 'GPU-first latencies', the measured latencies in docs/design/gpu-first.md), the release gate passing on all 261 stacks inside verify --tier rendered. Met: every drag tick on the GPU within a display frame on the Air 2S under Detail, Presence and a full Basic layer at Fit, 33% and 100%, under Dehaze at 24 and 60 MP at Fit and 100%, and a RAW white-balance drag and its release; a commit's frame at once and its picture at rest and counts as soon as the reference renderer's on the Air 2S and at 24 MP; a history return in 9 ms and Compare's exit in 19 to 21 ms to the frame; a sample through three spatial segments within its 100 ms target warm. Idle memory does not grow without captures; the 20 MB a capture is the window readback. Of the timing tier's components, run alone on a quiet host, the slider, settled histogram, burst and memory targets pass; idle CPU, launch and uncached 24 MP open miss. The 60 MP and masked picture-at-rest rows and the heavy export rows are TASK-012's, where they beat the same build's reference. Paint at 100%, trivial export, launch and uncached 24 MP open remain measured misses; native Windows and Linux remain unmeasured.

Accepted (docs/decisions.md): the picture, sample and export tolerances; fast reduced-source motion below 100% reports its differences while the picture at rest is strictly gated; softer budget-reduced motion at 100%, subject to explicit qualification; the counts cadence, GPU export with the reference option and fallback and whole-export restart, and owner work on the blocking pool.

acceptance_criteria: Every corpus stack is within the recorded limit for every output kind on the M4, recorded as the release gate's result; any other machine's result is recorded with its hardware.
Every latency above is recorded with p50/p95, load, build and source identity against its baseline; the known costs, the roadmap and feature status state the measured costs and nothing unmeasured.
Source files are unchanged after every run.

Softer budget-reduced motion at 100% has explicit native qualification with the affected stacks, views, drawing path and reported reference differences; acceptance of that behaviour is not itself evidence that it is qualified. Met: gpu-qualification reports the softer frame on every 100% cell, natural or forced, against the picture at rest and the reference (docs/specs/performance.md, The softer frame at 100%).

steps: Build release once, run the harness and each measurement sequentially on a quiet host, record and update the documents.
commands: cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- editor-latency --mode drag --source RAW --output NEW_DIR --samples 30
cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- editor-performance --source fixtures/generated/24mp.jpg --output NEW_DIR --samples 30
expected_results: The gate passes; the baseline costs are gone or named with their measured figures.

tasks.description: Make the GPU's picture at rest, its histogram and clipping counts, and the GPU export faster than the reference renderer on every measured row on the M4. Make the rest's tile charge match what its slot allocates, and give the rest a larger share. Keep Dehaze's light across tile-slot refits. Order the rest's tiles by window shape. Pipeline the export tile worker. Draw stacks with several spatial layers in staged sweeps, so a tile's window carries only its own layers' halos. Explain or fix paint at 100%. Attribute the launch and open misses. Let editor-latency pair held ticks. Render a developed photograph's catalog tiers (grid and large) on the GPU through the tile service.
extra_context: Design: docs/design/gpu-first.md and docs/design/gpu-preview.md describe the delivered staged sweeps, tile charges, pipelined export and catalog tiers. The measured throughput and remaining misses are in docs/specs/performance.md, GPU throughput against the reference.

Step 1 (lane B, wave 1). Files: ui rest.rs, light.rs, tiles.rs, photo_surface.rs; app gpu_preview.rs, gpu_tiles.rs; xtask/src/editor_latency.rs.
- Attribution figures: rest refits, lights encoded, retirement waits, window texels and a per-tile GPU span; the runner's upload, encode, wait and read times; per-tick rebinds and links run.
- Lights kept by key in a pipeline LRU of 8 one-texel textures, copied into a new pool.
- editor-latency pairs a path 'held' tick with its slider_draft_set and reports held inputs. A held input never drawn is superseded, not a failure.

Step 2 (lane A, wave 1). Files: core render/gpu/preview.rs and preview_tests.rs; app gpu_rest_tests.rs.
- tile_bytes matches the slot's allocation.
- The rest's share is 2 GiB less the source, the view plan and the accumulator, at most 1.25 GiB (REST_SHARE_MAX), by the plan's own figures (replacing REST_TILE_BYTES = 512 MiB).
- Rest tiles are ordered by window shape, row by row within a shape.
- A side whose window takes more than about 24 MP·links steps down.

Step 3 (lane B, wave 2). Files: ui tiles.rs, new gpu_preview/staged.rs; app gpu_tiles.rs.
- The tile worker holds the band's source rows, reuses its slot per window shape and keeps two tiles in flight. A call waits behind at most two tiles.
- The stage holder that steps 5 and 6 share: up to 2 x 2 textures of the content stage, a tile's rect copied in, a window copied out, charged before creation.

Step 4 (lane A, wave 2). Files: core render/gpu/preview.rs, render/gpu/tiles.rs, plan.rs; app gpu_plan.rs. Plan staged sweeps for RestTiles and StreamPlan, not yet drawn:
- Group the chain's links into sweeps, splitting before a spatial link only where the halos and leads before it pass about 64 px.
- Each sweep's tiles are windowed and anchored for its own links (anchor_of over its spatial slice).
- At most two stage textures, charged within the rest's share or the export budget. A stack that does not fit is planned chained.

Step 5 (lane A, wave 3). Files: ui rest.rs, gpu_preview.rs. The surface draws the rest in sweeps:
- Each sweep copies its tiles' rects of the last link's intermediate into a stage texture, and the next sweep cuts its boundaries from it.
- The last sweep reduces and counts as the chained rest does.
- The chained fallback is kept, and the stage textures retire with the rest.
Step 6 (lane B, wave 3). Files: ui tiles.rs; app gpu_tiles.rs. The runner draws streams in sweeps within GPU_TILE_BUDGET.

Step 7 (integrator, wave 4):
- verify --tier quick and rendered (the release gate).
- On a quiet M4, back to back with --reference-renderer: the 60 MP drag-stack commit, the Air 2S masked release, the Air 2S three-segment commit, and the 24 MP and Air 2S drag stacks; GPU against reference exports at 24 and 60 MP, trivial and heavy.
- Paint at 100% over the masked stack, with step 1's attribution.
- Launch split into spawn, first RSS, startup and first frame_captured; open split by decoded.reduced and the worker's render time, on the baseline build and the tip, interleaved and reversed, with syspolicyd's pid checked.
- The visibility smoke over a commit while minimized.
- Update gpu-preview.md, gpu-first.md, architecture.md limits, performance-rules.md, performance.md, features.md and development.md.

Step 8 (conditional, wave 5). If step 1 attributes paint's tail to word or block buffer regrowth forcing a re-evaluation (ui gpu_preview.rs:2293, 2662-2698): grow with headroom at a stroke's start, and rebind without forgetting unchanged content. Otherwise record the miss with its cause.

Compatibility with the visibility gating and job.wait:
- The rest stays on the frame clock, and no timer or poll is added.
- The pipelined tile worker blocks only its own thread.
- Export timings are read through job.wait, whose reader wakes on a changed or terminal record.

Settled (docs/decisions.md, GPU-first rendering): the export worker's budget GPU_TILE_BUDGET is 2 GiB, apart from the preview budget; an open's first picture is the GPU's view plan when its programs are warm, the reference frame only on a cold cache or without a GPU; whether a hidden window stops frames is verified, and if it does analysis.request answers from the reference while hidden; a developed photograph's catalog tiers render on the GPU through the tile service (previews/rendered.rs), exact within the display limit.

Build the exact light behind a spatial layer through the staged sweeps (the stand-in light passes the limits on a masked Dehaze behind Clarity on the Z6: worst block 4.8 ΔE00 at 100%, 4.5 in export), with the failing recipe in the corpus.

Measured on the M4 (release, quiet host; docs/specs/performance.md, GPU throughput against the reference). Met, the GPU's picture at rest and counts sooner than the same build's reference renderer at p50 and p95, both orders: the 60 MP drag stack's counts 0.60 to 0.62 s against 1.76 to 2.35 s, in 2 sweeps of 15 tiles of 2048 px; the Air 2S masked stroke's release 0.71 to 0.73 s against 1.30 to 1.42 s, in 4 sweeps of 42 tiles, the GPU-preview peak 2,146.5 MB of the 2 GiB budget; the Air 2S three-segment commit (a linear mask's masked Clarity) 0.31 to 0.34 s against 0.96 to 1.05 s; the 24 MP and Air 2S drag stacks 0.23 to 0.26 s and 0.26 to 0.27 s against 0.64 to 0.67 and 1.14 to 1.15 s; the X100VI 0.62 / 0.65 s against 2.43 / 2.56 s (no 60 MP RAW in the corpus). Exports, medians of five through job.wait: heavy 0.28 against 0.78 s at 24 MP and 0.63 against 2.02 s at 60 MP, the masked Air 2S stack 0.46 against 1.18 s in 24 tiles, the worker's peak 2.11 GB; missed: a trivial export 101 against 85 ms at 24 MP and 190 against 175 ms at 60 MP, not attributed. Drag ticks stay within a display frame, all on the GPU, none held. Missed: paint at 100% over the masked stack, p95 22.5 to 24.0 ms; the slow ticks run the same 5 links, 52 passes and 6.4 MP window as the fast ones with no refit or rebind, so H1 is refuted and step 8's buffer fix does not apply; they come in runs of 4 to 13 consecutive ticks on the third frame, not separated further. Launch and open, measured on this build and the baseline build interleaved and reversed: about 0.45 s of each is the host's on both builds; this build launches 0.18 to 0.23 s later before the process's first RSS sample (copying and first-checking a 52.0 MB executable against 35.5 MB) and 0.04 to 0.10 s later in the editor's start before its startup event; the 24 MP open is the same on both builds, its first picture the GPU's view plan when warm and its picture at rest in 6 tiles 70 to 90 ms after it; about 0.95 to 1.0 s of each launch and open lies between the first RSS sample and the startup event on both builds, unattributed. Idle 0.0% of one core after an open. Cold shader cache, 3 fresh bundles: the GPU's first frame 0.79 to 0.84 s after the reference's; the first fresh bundle's warm-up 2.09 s, the next two 0.68 s, the system compiler cache outside the bundle serving them. Catalog tiers: the GPU sooner on every row, the Z 6 with Presence 0.34 to 0.55 against 0.80 to 0.83 s. Remaining verification: quick and rendered after the throughput changes, including the release gate, and a commit while minimized followed by analysis.request, which the hidden-analysis scenario checks for a minimized and a hidden window, correlated by entry. gpu-preview.md describes the staged and light sweeps; architecture.md lists the 2 GiB tile-worker budget, and the development guide describes the configured lanes without supplying passing hosted results.

Accepted (docs/decisions.md): the release-compilation threshold, the first-photograph warm-up, at-most-four pixel-read replays and the host renderer for existing stored picks. The bounded RAW sensor pick reads 169 sites on the owner, an accepted exception. Neutral-picker answers name their renderer as renderer {record, reason}, tested through the desktop's GPU tile worker (gpu_tiles_worker_tests) and the headless reference (crates/luxforge-core/tests/basic/white_balance.rs) and documented in the user guide.

acceptance_criteria: On the M4, same release build, back to back with --reference-renderer: the GPU's picture at rest and its counts land sooner at p50 and p95 than the reference's frame and histogram for the 60 MP drag-stack commit, the Air 2S masked-stack release and the Air 2S three-segment commit; the 24 MP and Air 2S drag stacks are no worse than TASK-011 measured.
The GPU export's median is below the reference export's at 24 and 60 MP, trivial and heavy; the 60 MP heavy row is subject to Q1 and is recorded as an explained miss under the default.
Painting over the masked stack at 100% has p95 at or under 16 ms, or the tail is attributed from per-tick figures in docs/specs/performance.md.
Launch to an empty shell and the uncached 24 MP open return to 1,378 / 1,476 ms and 783 / 827 ms, or each regression's cause is named from split measurements of both builds.

Staged sweeps draw the same codes and counts as chained tiles, byte for byte, on the headless surface and the tile runner; the release gate passes on the whole corpus; GPU-preview and tile-worker peaks are recorded within their budgets; sources are unchanged.
editor-latency measures runs with held ticks, reporting their count and reasons, and still fails a set with no answer.
The neutral-picker answer names its renderer, with desktop GPU and headless/reference query tests and schema/user documentation.

steps: Agents run only their crates' filtered tests: the cross-crate charge parity, sweep planning, staged-against-chained byte equality on the headless surface and the runner, pipelined bands against sequential ones, light reuse across refits and held-tick pairing on synthetic logs.
The integrator runs the quick and rendered tiers once, then the timing runs on a quiet M4 with the load recorded, the reference renderer back to back and the launch and open splits on both builds.

cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- verify --tier rendered --output NEW_DIR
cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- editor-latency --source fixtures/generated/60mp.jpg --output NEW_DIR --mode commit --samples 30 --basic --detail --presence [--reference-renderer]

cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- editor-latency --source AIR2S.DNG --output NEW_DIR --mode paint --samples 240 --masks 3 --mask-presence --presence --detail [--zoom 100] [--reference-renderer]
cargo xtask develop --background --hidden-window --evidence-dir NEW_DIR --evidence-script EXPORTS.json --open SOURCE
expected_results: Every filtered test passes; staged and chained output are byte-identical; the release gate passes.
The rows in the acceptance criteria meet their targets or are recorded as explained misses with their scope, load and build identity.
